## What you should be able to do tonight

- Reproduce all six instrument definitions from memory with no more than one prompt each.
- Say which two of the six you understand least well, and what specifically is missing.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>35 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} Finish anything outstanding from days 1 to 6. The most common gap is the ETF creation-redemption sequence, because it is the only one that is a process rather than a definition.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Close every file. On one blank page, write the six instruments and for each: what it obliges you to do, what it obliges the other side to do, and the one thing that surprised you. Then open the glossary and mark what you missed.
:::
:::

## Drill <span class='task-total'>interview thread</span>

Spaced repetition, not cramming. Every drill in the year is collected on the [drills page](../drills.qmd).

::: {.task-list .drill}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Mental arithmetic baseline, and you will repeat this every drill day for a year, so write the numbers down. Ten two-digit multiplications against a 60-second clock, then 1/7 through 6/7 as decimals from memory, then 15 percent of 340 and 340 divided by 8. Record the time and the error count.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Counting, warm-up: how many distinct five-card poker hands contain exactly one pair? Get the number, then check it sums correctly against the total of 2,598,960 hands when you add the other categories from memory.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Conditional probability, the version that gets asked: a family has two children, at least one of whom is a boy born on a Tuesday. Probability both are boys? Do it by enumerating the sample space, and then say out loud why the Tuesday changes the answer at all.
:::
:::
